title: Signal · Wednesday 25 November
overview: A National Council committee backs 90 percent capital cover for UBS's foreign units, the SNB explores a Swiss Financial Ledger with eight partners, and the UK's cyber centre reports a rise in attacks by autonomous AI tools.

top.headline: Update: National Council committee backs 90 percent capital cover for UBS's foreign units
top.summary: The National Council's Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee voted on 24 November for UBS to back its foreign subsidiaries with 90 percent CET1 capital, in line with the Council of States. The option beat 80 percent by 13 votes to 12, and the Federal Council's 100 percent lost by 17 to 7, according to finews.
top.background: UBS must currently back 45 percent of these holdings with CET1, the Swiss Bankers Association said, calling 90 percent an enormous Swiss finish. In September UBS put the extra capital needed under that option at about USD 16 billion, finews reported.
top.why: With the ratio close to settled, the fight moves to valuation. The committee unanimously asked the Federal Council to study the equity method, which could lower the bill, AWP reported.
top.watch_next: The National Council debates the bill on 16 December, and the SP has threatened a referendum if Parliament softens it too far.

top.headline: SNB, UBS, SIX and six other firms explore a shared Swiss Financial Ledger
top.summary: The Swiss National Bank said on 24 November it has started an exploratory project with UBS, SIX, Zürcher Kantonalbank, PostFinance, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise, Basler Kantonalbank, Sygnum Bank and the settlement platform Seturion. They will assess whether one DLT platform, on which central bank money, commercial bank money and securities interact, could serve domestic and cross-border transactions.
top.background: The work sits within Project Helvetia, whose pilot of wholesale central bank money on the SIX Digital Asset Platform runs until at least June 2028, and builds on Project Agorá of the BIS and the IIF.
top.why: It puts the big bank, the exchange operator, PostFinance and three cantonal banks around one design for tokenised settlement, with governance on the table from the start. The SNB stressed that it is no sign a ledger will launch.
top.watch_next: What the new Helvetia Strategic Board, with the Swiss Bankers Association as observer, concludes on design and governance.

top.headline: UK cyber centre reports a marked rise in attacks by autonomous AI hacking tools
top.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said in a blog post that several incidents since September involved autonomous hacking tools and caused intrusions and downtime, according to TechCrunch on 24 November. The tools go after long-standing weaknesses such as exposed systems, weak passwords and API endpoints used by developers.
top.background: Free autonomous penetration testing tools such as Artex and Cairn appeared earlier this year, and the FBI has warned that attackers use them at unprecedented speed, TechCrunch reported.
top.why: The NCSC traced the weaknesses to years of technical debt, a familiar problem for banks with legacy estates, and said flaws unnoticed for years can now be found in minutes. It added that established controls still work, so basic hygiene on internet-facing systems matters more than ever.

items.headline: EIOPA expert group sets five principles for responsible data use in insurance
items.summary: EIOPA published on 24 November the report of its Consultative Expert Group on Data Use in Insurance. Its five principles cover access, fair and affordable outcomes, transparency and meaningful choice, prudential soundness and safe progress, and it asks supervisors to watch exclusion, affordability, explainability, bias and validation within existing rules.
items.why: Gives insurers building AI pricing and claims models an early view of what EU supervisors may look for, including accountability for third-party data and AI systems.

items.headline: XTX Markets unit sues Dell as AI server makers raise prices on existing orders
items.summary: Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are charging some customers up to 45 percent more for AI servers already ordered, mainly because memory chips cost more, according to the Financial Times as reported by Netzwoche. A Finnish subsidiary of trading firm XTX Markets has sued Dell in Ireland over an extra USD 62 million to 70 million on an order of about USD 549 million. Dell disputes its account.
items.why: Banks planning on-premise GPU clusters for data control face quotes that can move between order and delivery.

items.headline: EFG International reaches a record CHF 206.1 billion in assets as its margin narrows
items.summary: EFG International said on 24 November that net profit for the first ten months was about CHF 300 million, up around 10 percent excluding a 2025 insurance recovery. Assets under management hit a record CHF 206.1 billion and net new assets CHF 9.2 billion, a 6 percent annualised rate, while the revenue margin fell to 89 basis points from 95.
items.why: The adviser hiring and acquisition model keeps bringing in money, while quieter markets and clients squeeze revenue per franc managed.

items.headline: Swiss pension lump-sum payouts have almost doubled in ten years, FSO says
items.summary: The Federal Statistical Office said on 24 November that the number of people drawing new occupational pension benefits rose by more than 34 percent between 2015 and 2025. Amounts taken as a lump sum almost doubled over the decade, and a marked gender gap remains, according to its new pensions statistics.
items.why: More retirees leave the second pillar with capital to invest, which widens the market for retirement advice at banks and wealth managers.

items.headline: Former JPMorgan vice chairman Daniel Pinto joins the Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee
items.summary: The Chancellor has appointed Daniel Pinto, most recently Vice Chairman of JPMorgan Chase and before that its President and Chief Operating Officer, as an external member of the Financial Policy Committee, the Bank of England said on 24 November. His three-year term starts on 4 January 2027, replacing Jonathan Hall, after Treasury Committee scrutiny on 15 December.
items.why: Puts a career global markets banker on the UK's macroprudential regulator, which identifies and tackles systemic risks in British finance.

items.headline: Swiss Confederation cuts planned bond issuance to about CHF 3 billion in 2027
items.summary: The Federal Finance Administration plans to auction Confederation bonds with a nominal value of around CHF 3 billion in 2027, against CHF 4.5 billion in 2026, the SNB and the FFA said on 24 November. With CHF 2.9 billion maturing in June, bonds outstanding rise by only CHF 0.1 billion. The Confederation expects a funding requirement of around CHF 4.9 billion.
items.why: Thin net supply of federal bonds keeps long-dated franc assets tight for Swiss pension funds and insurers.

items.headline: Microsoft closes an Azure API Management flaw that may have exposed stored secrets
items.summary: Microsoft found on 18 November that an unauthorised party could have reached secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances and fixed it the next day, Netzwoche reported, citing BleepingComputer. Client secrets, subscription keys and management tokens may be affected; the v2 tier is not. Norway's security authority says the flaw may be linked to attacks on Equinor and Skagerak Energi.
items.why: Firms running APIs through the Classic tier should rotate stored credentials, because the fix does not invalidate secrets taken before it.

items.headline: MCP servers can now ship skills to Claude, with background tasks and sign-off prompts
items.summary: Anthropic said on 24 November that Skills over MCP is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code, so a server can publish skills that update with it. Tasks, for long-running work, and Elicitation, which pauses to ask a user for input or approval, are generally available, and File Uploads is coming. Claude Code 2.1.332, dated 25 November, adds skills from MCP servers.
items.why: Firms can distribute expertise along with their connectors, with nothing separate for users to install; Enterprise plans get it later.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Regulatory Audit or Client Intelligence could ship inside an MCP connector and stay current with it, once Enterprise plans get the feature.

items.headline: Claude artifacts can now be installed as Mac and Windows apps, in beta
items.summary: Anthropic began rolling out Install as app in beta on 24 November. An installed artifact runs in its own window, uses Claude and the user's connectors, and can send notifications. Permissions range from browser-only to full computer access, which is limited to apps the user or their organisation made. On Enterprise plans it stays off until an owner turns it on.
items.why: Turns an artifact into a small internal tool people open daily, while admins keep control of what it can touch.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Atelier prototypes built as artifacts could open as desktop apps for demos, with permissions set for each app.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic shares fall below their USD 83 IPO price as AI stocks slide
items.summary: Anthropic's stock traded as low as USD 76 by midday on 24 November, below its USD 83 IPO price and down nearly 12 percent from Monday's close, according to TechCrunch. Nvidia fell more than 7 percent by midday, giving back part of Monday's rally after Jensen Huang's reinstatement.
items.why: Investors treat Anthropic's shares as a gauge for the sector, so a weak run could squeeze valuations and listing plans across the AI vendors banks buy from.

items.headline: OpenAI says GPT-6 models design proteins without specialised biology models
items.summary: OpenAI said on 24 November that its GPT-6 models can design new protein shapes and sequences using only reasoning and code. Its latest models performed comparably to or better than specialised models on most of 14 tasks, though full structure prediction remained a weakness, and lab tests with Onava showed evidence of binding across five targets.
items.why: Adds to the evidence that one general model can take over work that needed several specialist tools, which changes how firms plan their model estates.

say_it_today: On the day a parliamentary committee backed tougher capital rules for UBS's foreign units, the SNB brought UBS into a study of a shared Swiss DLT ledger. Switzerland is tightening its big bank's balance sheet while redesigning the market plumbing it runs on.
